source: English Wikipedia; all titles verified via MediaWiki API (redirects resolved to final titles)

conventions.women_first_record_year: earliest women's mark listed in the Wikipedia progression table (unofficial/pre-recognition included)
conventions.women_official_year: first year the governing body ratified women's records: FSFI (1922-36, absorbed by IAAF 1936) then IAAF/World Athletics; FINA/World Aquatics for swimming
conventions.sections: section_men / section_women name the Wikipedia section(s) holding the outdoor (athletics) or long-course (swimming) table

events.section_men: Records 1912–1976 + Records since 1977 (also 'Unofficial progression before the IAAF' from 1891)
events.section_women: Records 1922–1976 + Records from 1975
events.comparable_note: Same distance/conditions. Hand-timed vs FAT split: IAAF accepted FAT separately from 1975 and required it from 1977; tables split pre-/post-1977.
events.doping_note: W: Griffith Joyner 10.49 (1988) still standing; wind-gauge dispute and era suspicion, never a positive test; GDR sprinters hold 1970s-80s marks. M: Ben Johnson 1987/88 marks rescinded; current men's WR Bolt 2009.
events.notes: Women's 1922 = FSFI (Fédération Sportive Féminine Internationale); FSFI absorbed by IAAF 1936. Some early marks are 100 y/110 y.

events.section_men: Outdoor (Records 1951–1976 / Records post-1977)
events.section_women: Outdoor (Records 1922–36; 1951–76 / Records from 1977)
events.comparable_note: Same distance. Straight-track 200 m records existed until 1976; IAAF curve-200 record category from 1951 (both sexes). Use 'Outdoor' sections, ignore 'Indoor'.
events.doping_note: W: Griffith Joyner 21.34 (1988) still standing; Koch (GDR) marks 1979-84. M: Bolt 19.19 (2009).
events.notes: Women's 1922 = FSFI (straight-track era); IAAF curve records only from 1951, so a clean comparable series starts 1951.

events.section_men: Outdoor (Records 1895–1976 / Records post-1976)
events.section_women: Outdoor (Record progression 1957–1974 / Record progression from 1975)
events.comparable_note: Same distance. Use Outdoor tables; 440 y marks accepted early.
events.doping_note: W: Marita Koch (GDR) 47.60 (1985) still standing — archetypal state-doping-era record; Kratochvílová 47.99 (1983). M: Van Niekerk 43.03 (2016).
events.notes: Women's outdoor table starts at IAAF recognition 1957 (indoor table from 1951). No FSFI-era 400 m series.

events.section_men: Men > Outdoor
events.section_women: Women > Outdoor
events.comparable_note: Same distance. Combined page. Women's Olympic 800 m held 1928, then dropped until 1960.
events.doping_note: W: Kratochvílová (TCH) 1:53.28 (1983) — longest-standing individual athletics WR, doping-era suspicion. Koubek's 1930s marks rescinded (noted on page). M: Rudisha 1:40.91 (2012).
events.notes: Women's 1922 = FSFI; first rows include 880 y and en-route marks.

events.section_men: Men (outdoors) > Pre-IAAF + IAAF era
events.section_women: Women (outdoors) > Pre-IAAF + IAAF era
events.comparable_note: Same distance. Combined page.
events.doping_note: W: Qu Yunxia (CHN) 3:50.46 (1993 Chinese National Games, 'Ma's Army') stood until 2015 — 1993 Chinese distance marks widely doubted; Kazankina (URS) 1980. M: El Guerrouj 3:26.00 (1998).
events.notes: Women's pre-IAAF series starts 1927 (Soviet marks); IAAF first ratified women's 1500 m in 1967.

events.section_men: Men > Pre-IAAF (Professionals / Amateurs) + IAAF / World Athletics era
events.section_women: Women > Pre-IAAF + Women's IAAF era
events.comparable_note: Same distance. Combined page; not an Olympic event. Ignore indoor and 'Road' sections (road mile WRs only since Sept 2023).
events.doping_note: W: Masterkova (RUS) 4:12.56 (1996) stood until 2019. Sparse women's series; elite women rarely race the mile.
events.notes: Women's pre-IAAF from 1921 (Elizabeth Atkinson, GBR); IAAF ratification from 1967 (Anne Smith). Men's professional marks from 1850s complicate the men's baseline.

events.section_men: Men > Outdoor (Pre-IAAF era, to 1912 / IAAF era, from 1912)
events.section_women: Women > Outdoor (Pre-IAAF, to 1974 / IAAF era, from 1974)
events.comparable_note: Same distance. Combined page. Men's individual 3000 m never Olympic (team race 1912–24 only); women's Olympic 1984–1992, replaced by 5000 m in 1996.
events.doping_note: W: Wang Junxia (CHN) 8:06.11 (1993) still standing — Chinese 1993 distance records widely doubted. M: Ingebrigtsen 7:17.55 (2024).
events.notes: Women's 1927 row (Cicanei) is isolated; continuous series from 1954. IAAF from 1974 (Bragina).

events.section_men: Men > Pre-World Athletics + World Athletics era
events.section_women: Women > Pre-recognition + World Athletics world records
events.comparable_note: Same distance. Combined page.
events.doping_note: W: series begins 1981 (short history); Chinese 1997 marks in progression. Super-spike era (c.2019+) affects both sexes.
events.notes: Women's pre-recognition marks from 1969 (Pigni).

events.section_men: Men > Pre-IAAF + IAAF world records
events.section_women: Women > Pre-recognition + IAAF world records
events.comparable_note: Same distance. Combined page.
events.doping_note: W: Wang Junxia (CHN) 29:31.78 (1993) stood until 2016 — doubtful 1993 mark distorts the gap for 23 years. Current W: Chebet 28:54.14 (2024). Super-spike era affects both.
events.notes: Women's pre-recognition from 1966 (GDR marks, year-only dates); IAAF from 1981.

events.section_men: Men
events.section_women: Women
events.comparable_note: Same distance (42.195 km standardized 1921). Combined page. Women's records split mixed-race vs 'Women Only' (rule passed 2011, retroactive to 2007): use mixed for comparability with men. Course eligibility rules apply to both.
events.doping_note: Pacing and super-shoe era (2017+) affect both sexes. W: Chepng'etich 2:09:56 (2024) is the listed WR; she was suspended in 2025 for a positive test on a later sample — re-verify record status. Kosgei 2:14:04 (2019).
events.notes: World Athletics credits Violet Piercy (1926) as first woman at full distance; page also lists Marie-Louise Ledru 1918 (ARRS). Before 1 Jan 2004 marathon marks were 'world bests'; road WRs ratified from 2004 (same for men).

events.section_men: Men
events.section_women: Women > Pre-IAAF recognition + IAAF ratified
events.comparable_note: Barrier height differs: men 91.4 cm, women 76.2 cm. Ratio not meaningful.
events.doping_note: W: very short series (from 1996) with rapid 'new event' improvement.
events.notes: Women's event recognized as of 1 Jan 2000 with Motalova's 1999 9:48.88 as inaugural record. Men's event standardized 1954.

events.wiki_women: Women's high jump world record progression

events.section_women: Record progression > Outdoor
events.comparable_note: Same rules/bar. Use outdoor tables.
events.doping_note: W: Kostadinova (BUL) 2.09 (1987) stood until Mahuchikh 2.10 (2024) — era record. M: Sotomayor 2.45 (1993) still standing. Fosbury flop adoption (c.1968-78) affects both.
events.notes: Women's 1922 = FSFI.

events.wiki_men: Men's pole vault world record progression
events.wiki_women: Women's pole vault world record progression
events.section_men: Record progression
events.section_women: Pre-IAAF Record Progression + IAAF Record Progression
events.comparable_note: Same rules. But men's pole technology changes (bamboo -> steel -> fibreglass, 1950s-60s) happened before the women's event existed, so women started on modern poles. Indoor marks count since 2000 for both.
events.doping_note: No doping-era issue, but strong 'new event' effect: women's record rose ~1 m 1992-2005. Pre-IAAF women's marks (from 1910) are sparse and amateur.
events.notes: IAAF recognized women's PV in 1994; inaugural record Sun Caiyun 4.05 (1992).

events.section_men: Men > Outdoor
events.section_women: Women > Outdoor (Unofficial pre-IAAF progression to 1990 / Official IAAF progression from 1990)
events.comparable_note: Same rules. Combined page.

events.notes: IAAF recognized women's TJ in 1990.

events.comparable_note: Same distance and rules, but no Wikipedia world-record progression page exists. Checked and missing: '20 kilometres race walk world record progression', "Men's/Women's 20 kilometres race walk world record progression", 'Racewalking world record progression'. The article '20 kilometres race walk' has current WRs only.
events.doping_note: Russian race-walking doping scandal (2010s; Lashmanova's faster time never ratified). Judging (loss of contact) is subjective.
events.notes: Women walked 10 km at the Olympics 1992-96 and 20 km from 2000. Road-walk WRs only ratified since the early 2000s. Recommend exclusion.
